title: AI ROI: Move From Minutes Saved To Value Created
summary: The report “Artificial Intelligence ROI: Productivity Plus Adaptive Advantage” challenges enterprises to look beyond the productivity promise.
body_markdown:
What if your employees work faster with AI but your business still fails to earn a return? Minutes saved make a persuasive demonstration but do not, on their own, prove that an investment creates value.


Our research,


[Artificial Intelligence ROI: Productivity Plus Adaptive Advantage](https://www.forrester.com/report/artificial-intelligence-roi-productivity-plus-adaptive-advantage/RES205568) , challenges enterprises to look beyond the productivity promise.


Workflow redesign matters, but the bigger opportunity is adaptive advantage: using AI to improve decisions, accelerate experimentation, drive revenue, strengthen resilience, and respond to changing customer needs.


The question is not simply, “How much work can AI automate?” but rather, “How will AI make this enterprise more valuable and more adaptable?”


## Three Findings That Challenge The AI Payback Story


- **Adoption is not the same as transformation.** Enterprise AI adoption is strong, particularly among large businesses and knowledge-intensive sectors, yet only about a fifth of US enterprises (with 250 or more employees who use AI) are developing new workflows to use AI in business processes. Adding an assistant to an unchanged process is not enough. Leaders need to rethink task sequencing, handoffs, and human oversight so that individual time savings translate into better enterprise outcomes. Forrester’s


[AIQ 2.0: Employees (Still) Aren’t Ready To Succeed With Workforce AI](https://www.forrester.com/report/aiq-2-0-employees-still-arent-ready-to-succeed-with-workforce-ai/RES192767) complements workflow redesign by highlighting gaps in employees’ AI understanding, skills, and ethics and the need to benchmark workforce readiness.


- **Productivity alone sets a demanding hurdle.** The report brings together estimates of AI productivity uplift by 2035 that range from 1.5% to 2.6% of US GDP, averaging around 2%. These are expectations, not realized returns. Historical technology waves like the creation of the personal computer or the creation of the World Wide Web took years to deliver sustained productivity improvements.[Forrester’s AI Impact Returns Navigator tool](https://www.forrester.com/report/artificial-intelligence-roi-productivity-plus-adaptive-advantage/RES205568) explores the cost-return trade-offs of different adoption scenarios. Its central challenge for leaders: Gains must be large enough and arrive soon enough to outweigh investment costs on a net-present-value basis.


- **AI economics extend beyond the model.** Cloud compute, software, equipment, power, cooling, and non-IT costs shape the return alongside productivity, considering that only


[10% to 25% of total AI spend is attributable to models](https://www.tokeneconomics.com/insights/total-cost-of-ai-tca/) . More demanding deployments can raise consumption, while usage-based pricing makes spending sensitive to how AI is used. At the same time, value can come from better decisions, faster innovation, increased revenues, and greater organizational resilience. Those adaptive gains are part of investment returns, even when they do not immediately increase output per worker. A narrow efficiency scorecard risks overlooking them.


## What It Means


- **Manage AI as a portfolio of value, not a collection of pilots.** Pair near-term productivity initiatives with use cases that improve customer engagement, create new offerings, or help the business adapt to new markets. For each investment, define the value using the


[Forrester AI Value Matrix](https://www.forrester.com/report/introducing-the-forrester-ai-value-matrix-a-framework-for-measuring-what-matters/RES194340) and specify the outcome, accountable owner, expected timing, and evidence needed to demonstrate value. Use the[navigator tool](https://www.forrester.com/report/artificial-intelligence-roi-productivity-plus-adaptive-advantage/RES205568) to challenge assumptions about adoption speed, benefit growth, and funding costs rather than treating a favorable scenario as a forecast. Connect those decisions through


[cross-functional governance](https://www.forrester.com/report/high-performance-it-makes-business-results-technologys-north-star/RES165697) so that teams share priorities, expose overlapping spending, and redeploy capital toward use cases that prove their worth.


- **Make measurement as adaptive as the technology.** Track output per worker, but also test whether AI improves decision quality, experimentation, customer outcomes, resilience, and revenues. Match models to tasks: A smaller, cheaper model may be sufficient for classification, while more complex reasoning may justify a more capable option. Monitor consumption and cloud commitments as deployments scale. Revisit the business case when costs, workflows, or realized benefits change, and consider outcome-based engagements. The goal is not the most impressive demonstration or the largest volume of AI activity. It is a disciplined path to measurable returns that’s outcome-focused and supported by an enterprise that can learn and change.


[Introducing The Forrester AI Value Matrix: A Framework For Measuring What Matters](https://www.forrester.com/report/introducing-the-forrester-ai-value-matrix-a-framework-for-measuring-what-matters/RES194340) provides a common language for assessing AI value across functions, financial categories, and maturity levels.
